fix: had been the first to attack him
reason: τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιβάλλει αὐτῷ: Ptolemy attacks Antiochus first; 'territory not his' is invented. 'Attack' avoids the arrest sense of 'lay hands on'.

fix: saying that [...] he would make Gentius well disposed
reason: Lacuna after ἐξιγμένον; 'somehow' papers over the gap.
ἐξελεγχθῆναι = be exposed or proved wanting (shown to be bribable), not 'won over'; 'put to the proof' loses the failure.
καλῶς ποιῶν is the idiom 'happily, and a good thing too'; 'by good fortune' gives that sense. Polybius is not praising Perseus.

fix: only a very few Greeks were guilty of utter folly at the crisis of the action
reason: Passive ἠλογήθησαν is unclear: 'acted foolishly' (Paton) fits context, 'were disregarded' is possible. 'Driven' is unsupported either way.

fix: word reached the Achaeans concerning King Ptolemy that the customary rites performed for kings when they come of age, the Anacleteria, had now taken place in his case
reason: Impersonal προσπεσόντος = news arrived, Ptolemy did not apply; διότι = 'that'. Named ἀνακλητήρια restored without parentheses.

fix: he was to send his fellow envoys off at once to report this
reason: Polybius is the subject of πέμπειν (contrast αὐτὸν δέ); his colleagues are the ones sent.
Ἀλκίθον is the accusative of Ἀλκίθος.

fix: Agesilochus son of Hegesias, Nicagoras and Nicander were sent to Rome
reason: Three envoys are listed; Nicander is not Nicagoras' father.

fix: those of the envoys from Greece who had been sent to arrange a settlement came to meet him
reason: Partitive genitive: a single group, the Greek envoys sent to arrange peace, who then speak.
